- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > history peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +20% above recent peak or adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment turns negative.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment volatility > 0.5.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast with sentiment average over 3–5 periods.
